table_guide.what: What each department is asking Parliament for, broken down by vote. The headline number.
Why they are asking for more money mid-year. One line per request, naming the initiative.
The named grants and contributions going out the door. Which program, how much.

table_guide.table: Expenditures by Purpose (also "by Program or Purpose")
table_guide.what: Which actual program the money lands in, rather than which department. This is how you follow money to a purpose instead of a mailbox.
What the money is spent on: salaries, professional services, transfer payments, equipment. Spending by category instead of by department.
Spending already authorized by existing law, so Parliament does not vote on it. Reported for information only. Usually the biggest number in the document.
Money leaving one department's vote and landing in another's. The hardest thing to follow in federal spending, and no longer published at all.

table_guide.table: Allocations from Treasury Board Central Votes
table_guide.what: Money Treasury Board released from its own pots before Parliament voted on it: contingencies, pay adjustments, carry-forwards. The single most sensitive table in the set.
Initiatives funded across several departments at once, grouped so you can see the full cost of one program.
Money that was approved but locked and cannot be spent.
